title: Rigveda 8.85: To Asvins
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 8.85: To Asvins: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 8.85 is a hymn of 9 verses addressed to Asvins. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 8, the book of the Kaṇva and Aṅgiras poets. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 650v-651r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 8.85.1-8 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 6, varga 7); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 650v
translation.original_text:
1ā me̱ hava̍ṁ nāsa̱tyāśvi̍nā̱ gaccha̍taṁ yu̱vam | madhva̱ḥ soma̍sya pī̱taye̍ ||
2i̱mam me̱ stoma̍m aśvine̱mam me̍ śṛṇuta̱ṁ hava̍m | madhva̱ḥ soma̍sya pī̱taye̍ ||
3a̱yaṁ vā̱ṁ kṛṣṇo̍ aśvinā̱ hava̍te vājinīvasū | madhva̱ḥ soma̍sya pī̱taye̍ ||
4śṛ̱ṇu̱taṁ ja̍ri̱tur hava̱ṁ kṛṣṇa̍sya stuva̱to na̍rā | madhva̱ḥ soma̍sya pī̱taye̍ ||
5cha̱rdir ya̍nta̱m adā̍bhya̱ṁ viprā̍ya stuva̱te na̍rā | madhva̱ḥ soma̍sya pī̱taye̍ ||
6gaccha̍taṁ dā̱śuṣo̍ gṛ̱ham i̱tthā stu̍va̱to a̍śvinā | madhva̱ḥ soma̍sya pī̱taye̍ ||
7yu̱ñjāthā̱ṁ rāsa̍bha̱ṁ rathe̍ vī̱ḍva̍ṅge vṛṣaṇvasū | madhva̱ḥ soma̍sya pī̱taye̍ ||
8tri̱va̱ndhu̱reṇa̍ tri̱vṛtā̱ rathe̱nā yā̍tam aśvinā | madhva̱ḥ soma̍sya pī̱taye̍ ||
translation.text:
1To this mine invocation, O ye Aṣvins, ye Nâsatyas, come, To drink the savoury Soma juice.
2This laud of mine, ye Aṣvins Twain, and this mine invitation hear, To drink the savoury Soma juice.
3Here Kr̥ishṇa is invoking you, O Aṣvins, Lords of ample wealth. To drink the savoury Soma juice.
4List, Heroes, to the singer's call, the call of Kr̥ishṇa lauding you, To drink the savoury Soma juice.
5Chiefs, to the sage who sings your praise grant an inviolable home, To drink the savoury Soma juice.
6Come to the worshipper's abode, Aṣvins, who here is lauding you, To drink the savoury Soma juice.
7Yoke to the firmly jointed car the ass which draws you, Lords of wealth. To drink the savoury Soma juice.
8Come hither, Aṣvins, on your car of triple form with triple seat, To drink the savoury Soma juice.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 650v (numbered 72v by the scribe) (OPenn image 651, upper leaf). translation.original_text: <sup>9</sup>nū me̱ giro̍ nāsa̱tyāśvi̍nā̱ prāva̍taṁ yu̱vam | madhva̱ḥ soma̍sya pī̱taye̍ ||
translation.text: <sup>9</sup>O Aṣvins, O Nâsatyas, now accept with favouring grace my songs, To drink the savoury Soma juice.
